title: 3.4.15 Chart the Code: Decision Tree for Form Choice
description: Chart the rule for choosing between a declaration, an expression, and an arrow: is it a main operation called from several places, and is its body a single expression?

aiGrader.prompt: This chart is scored entirely by rules from its shapes and arrows. No model reads it.

rubric.title: A second question follows the first
rubric.description: Scored by the editor (arrow order): one decision comes before another on the route.

steps.fail: The rule asks two questions, one after the other. Draw a second diamond that comes after the first one.
steps.pass: The second question follows the first.

rubric.title: Three forms to choose from
rubric.description: Scored by the editor (shape kind): at least three task rectangles, one for each way to write the function.

steps.fail: There are three ways to write the function (a declaration, a one-line arrow, an arrow with a block body). Draw a task rectangle for each.
steps.pass: There is a task for each form.

rubric.title: A rule, not a repeat
rubric.description: Scored by the editor (arrow order): no decision is part of a repeat.

steps.fail: This is a decision tree, so no arrow should lead back to a diamond. In your chart one does.
steps.pass: No arrow leads back to a diamond.

rubric.title: The questions are about the functions
rubric.description: Scored by the editor: at least two diamonds ask about the function (where it is called, or what its body is).

steps.fail: Ask each question about the function itself: where it is called from, and what its body looks like.
steps.pass: The diamonds ask about the function.

gate.fail: None of your shapes say what this program does. Label each shape in your own words.
